meta.title: Star quest: campaign
meta.note: Every week cites the same source as the 12-week plan in star-quest-course. Week 5 is the one week with no page number behind it, flagged there and here.

regions.name: Weather Coast
regions.desc: Now against this morning — listening right to the end
regions.entry: The sky here changes its mind halfway through a sentence. Listen to the end.
regions.teacherNote: Present tense, “now” against “this morning” — the exact trap that beat her listening run

regions.name: Vowel Hollow
regions.desc: The spelling log, vowel teams, and the quiet middle syllable
regions.entry: Some vowels hide. You cannot hear them, and they are still there.
regions.teacherNote: The spelling log, vowel teams, and the quiet middle syllable that turned camera into camroa

regions.name: Story Marsh
regions.desc: Opposites, and signs that mean the opposite of the sentence
regions.entry: Read the sign, not the situation. A shop with a door can still be closed.
regions.teacherNote: Opposites, and signs that mean the opposite of what the sentence said

regions.name: Ceiling Peak
regions.desc: Push every skill past the point where the test ran out of questions
regions.entry: Nobody found the top of this one last time. Let us go and look.
regions.teacherNote: Push every skill past the point where the test simply ran out of questions

regions.name: The Summit
regions.desc: All four skills at once — the real paper, then the real test again
regions.teacherNote: All four skills at once — the real paper, then the real test again

weeks.title: Weather, seasons, and the word “now”
weeks.why: Unit 7's listening words are literally weather, cloudy, sunny, windy, snowy, rainy, and its grammar point is Simple Present with It. It is the closest thing in the book to the item she missed.
weeks.ket: KET Listening Part 1 — this is the Sample Test 1 Q4 item itself.

quests.title: Ten skies
quests.sub: Listen to the end. Every clip changes its mind.

quests.title: Weather words
quests.sub: Match the word to the sky.

quests.title: It is, it isn’t
quests.sub: Simple present with It.

weeks.title: Was, then is — the tense flip
weeks.source: Oxford Discover 1, Units 15 & 16 — “Percussion Instruments,” “Let’s Make Music!” (p.146, 156)
weeks.why: “It's raining” is present continuous, and the missed item turns entirely on the handover from was to is …ing. Units 15 and 16 are the book's present-continuous pair.
weeks.ket: Listening Parts 1 and 2, where the wrong option is almost always something that was true a moment ago.

quests.title: Before or now
quests.sub: Sort ten sentences into was and is doing.

quests.title: The band is playing
quests.sub: Percussion words, present continuous.

quests.title: Wait for the end
quests.sub: Six clips. The answer is never the first word.

boss.name: The Weather Wizard
boss.built: He only accepts sentences that mark the time correctly — what it was this morning against what it is now.

weeks.title: Start the spelling log
weeks.source: Oxford Discover Writing and Spelling 1, Spelling Master Class Units 1 & 2 (p.40, 41)
weeks.why: Unit 1 of the Master Class is, precisely, “keep a spelling log.” Unit 2 opens the vowel-team work with a_e / ay / ai — cake, birthday, paint.
weeks.ket: Reading & Writing Part 6 is scored on spelling alone — the right word spelt wrong scores nothing.

quests.title: Entry one: camera
quests.sub: The word that started the log.

quests.title: a_e, ay, ai
quests.sub: Three ways to write the same sound.

quests.title: Log check
quests.sub: Spell them without the letters laid out for you.

weeks.title: The many ways to write e
weeks.source: Oxford Discover Writing and Spelling 1, Spelling Master Class Unit 4 (p.43) — e, ea, ee, ey, y
weeks.why: The letter she skipped in camera was e. This is the book's e page: me, pea, see, key, baby.
weeks.ket: Part 6 again, and Part 2, where a misspelt answer scores zero even when the word chosen is right.

quests.title: Twelve e words
quests.sub: Hear it, then build it.

quests.title: Which e?
quests.sub: e, ea, ee, ey or y.

quests.title: Camera, cold
quests.sub: No hints this time.

weeks.title: The quiet middle syllable
weeks.source: Supplement — the Master Class covers e and o spellings (p.43, p.46) but has no page on unstressed vowels
weeks.why: Cam-er-a is three syllables and the middle one is swallowed; the same trap sits in family, every, different, chocolate, favourite. She needs to know the quiet vowel is there even when she cannot hear it.
weeks.ket: Part 6 build-the-word items are drawn from exactly this band of everyday three-syllable nouns.

quests.title: Clap the syllables
quests.sub: How many beats in the word?

quests.title: Find the quiet one
quests.sub: Which vowel is hiding?

quests.title: Write it anyway
quests.sub: Fifteen words with a swallowed middle.

boss.name: The Spelling Log
boss.built: Every word she has misspelt in this campaign, served back to her — starting with the one that opened the log.

weeks.title: Opposites
weeks.source: Oxford Discover 1, Unit 1 — Word Study: Opposites (p.6)
weeks.why: “Not open” → “closed” is one antonym step, and it is the step she skipped when she chose PUSH THE DOOR. The book puts Opposites in its very first Word Study box.
weeks.ket: Reading & Writing Part 1 notices are often a single word that is the opposite of the sentence you were given.

quests.title: Not X means Y
quests.sub: Twenty pairs, one step each.

quests.title: The shop again
quests.sub: Her exact missed item, cold.

quests.title: Opposite or just different?
quests.sub: The trap is the word that repeats.

weeks.title: Can’t, shouldn’t, must not
weeks.source: Oxford Discover 1, Units 17 & 18 — “Living and Nonliving Things,” “The Gingerbread Man” (p.166, 176)
weeks.why: She already does this well: she matched “You cannot bring your dog in here” to NO DOGS and “You must not make a noise here” to PLEASE BE QUIET, both right. Units 17 and 18 give her the grammar underneath.
weeks.ket: Part 1 is built almost entirely from can't / shouldn't / must not phrasing.

quests.title: Fifteen notices
quests.sub: Spelt-out rules mixed with one-word signs.

quests.title: Say the rule
quests.sub: Can't, shouldn't, must not.

quests.title: One word only
quests.sub: The sign never says the whole sentence.

boss.name: The Sign Reader
boss.built: A wall of notices. Read each one for what it means, not for the place it belongs to.

weeks.title: “It doesn’t say” — reading for what is absent
weeks.source: Oxford Discover 1, Units 13 & 14 — “Using Labels to Clarify Details” and “Understanding Contrast” (p.126, 136)
weeks.why: Given “Nina has a sister,” she answered “It doesn't say” — correct, and the hardest of the three options to choose. That instinct is worth pushing onto longer texts rather than re-teaching.
weeks.ket: Reading & Writing Part 4, right / wrong / doesn't say, at full A2 text length.

quests.title: Right, wrong, doesn’t say
quests.sub: Three short texts.

quests.title: Longer now
quests.sub: Three A2-length texts.

quests.title: Prove it
quests.sub: Which line of the text told you?

weeks.title: Listening Part 2, five speakers at once
weeks.source: Oxford Discover 1, Units 11 & 12 — Simple Present questions with Does (p.106, 116)
weeks.why: She answered the A1+ matching item correctly and was never offered a harder one. Units 11 and 12 build the question forms that Part 2 matching runs on.
weeks.ket: KET Listening Part 2 — five speakers matched against a list, a real step up from the single-clip Part 1 items she saw.

quests.title: Does he? Does she?
quests.sub: The question forms Part 2 runs on.

quests.title: Five speakers
quests.sub: First full Part 2 set.

quests.title: Five more
quests.sub: Second set. The rule still stands.

weeks.title: Word study sweep
weeks.source: Oxford Discover 1, Word Study — irregular plurals (Unit 5, p.46), compound nouns (Unit 7, p.66), adjectives (Unit 17, p.166)
weeks.why: The Word Study boxes are the book's word-shape strand and the nearest thing in it to what Part 6 asks for. Units 7 and 17 appear earlier in this plan for their grammar; this week uses a different column of the same pages.
weeks.ket: Reading & Writing Part 2 (best word) and Part 6 (build the word).

quests.title: One, then many
quests.sub: Irregular plurals.

quests.title: Two words, one thing
quests.sub: Compound nouns.

quests.title: The best word
quests.sub: Twenty items pitched at A2 Key.

boss.name: The Ceiling Climb
boss.built: One level above where the diagnostic stopped, in every skill at once. Nothing here is below A2 Key.

weeks.title: A full paper, timed properly
weeks.source: Cambridge KET for Schools Sample Test 1 — the paper several diagnostic items were drawn from
weeks.why: Everything so far has isolated one skill. This is the first time they run together under exam conditions, and the first honest read on stamina.

quests.title: Reading & Writing
quests.sub: Parts 1, 2 and 4, in order.

quests.title: Listening
quests.sub: Parts 1 and 2, with a minimum time per item.

quests.title: Build the word
quests.sub: Part 6, scored on spelling alone.

weeks.title: Retake star quest
weeks.why: Same instrument, same adaptive engine, comparable numbers. Compare ceilings first and percentages second — 85% can barely move while three ceilings rise.
weeks.ket: Direct — it is the exam-format instrument itself.

quests.title: Warm the engine
quests.sub: Six items, one from each region.

quests.title: The rule, one last time
quests.sub: Say it out loud before you start.

boss.name: The Summit
boss.built: The real star quest, unmodified, so the numbers compare honestly against 20 August.

badges.name: Tense Detective
badges.why: Answer six gated listening items in a row without rushing the gate.

badges.name: Vowel Hunter
badges.why: Three clean spelling items in a row — the quiet-vowel gap from Vowel Hollow.

badges.name: Sign Reader
badges.why: Read a full wall of notices with nothing wrong.

badges.name: Ceiling Breaker
badges.why: Answer four A2 items correctly in reading AND four in listening — the two ceilings the test never found.

badges.name: Log Keeper
badges.why: Beat the Spelling Log with every word it threw at you.

badges.name: Summiteer
badges.why: Finish all twelve weeks and stand on the Summit.
